text:
nina: quick design thought: instead of a flat grace credit, what if admission issues a short-lived weighted token grant based on org weight + recent success rate? aims: smooth cold bursts while preserving fairness for high-paying tenants.

jordan: hmm, weighted grants sounds promising. how do we compute weight? commit size? recent qps?

nina: idea: weight = alpha*committed_capacity + beta*rolling_success_rate(1m). normalized across orgs in region. small floor so tiny orgs still get minimal access.

carlos: calculation in the admission path will add CPU. need to keep admission cheap. can we precompute weights in a sliding window job and cache per-minute?

zane: yes cache + TTL of 30s. admission reads cached grant multiplier and issues tokens: grant = base_tokens * multiplier. base_tokens tuned by region.

priya: abuse vector: churn accounts could fake success_rate by spinning up quick requests that succeed. guard: success_rate should discount short-lived sessions and require token age > 10s for counting. also require recent billing activity for larger multipliers.

jordan: operational metrics we need: grant_issued_count, grant_size_histogram, grant_revoke_events, grant_abuse_flag. also a per-org "weight_adjust_reason" tag: (COMMIT_CHANGE, USAGE_SPIKE, MANUAL_OVERRIDE).

nina: proto sketch: ```proto
message TokenGrant {
  string org_id = 1;
  int32 tokens = 2; // ephemeral, not billed
  double multiplier = 3;
  int64 expires_at = 4;
  enum Reason {BASE = 0; WEIGHTED = 1; RECOVERY = 2;}
  Reason reason = 5;
}
```

carlos: interface boundary: admission returns TokenGrant; runtime must respect tokens as best-effort and still subject to local batch/coalescing. runtime should emit "grant_consumed" events.

zane: fairness note: normalize multiplier with a soft cap so large customers can't starve small ones. e.g., cap multiplier at 4x by default, adjustable by enterprise SKU.

priya: rollout: start with internal tenants in us-west, 1% traffic, monitor cpu. introduce a hard circuit-breaker: if region CPU > 75% and grant_consumed_rate rising, auto-scale down grants to base. infra-bot: confirm auto-scale hook exists?

infra-bot: hook confirmed: auto-scale-policy 'admission-grant-throttle' available. will need mapping from grant metrics -> scale action.

jordan: testing: synthetic workload: mix of 10k small tenants + 50 large tenants. validate tail latency, grant_abuse_rate < 0.5%, and small tenants median latency doesn't regress.

nina: other tradeoffs: increases complexity in admission; benefits: fewer 429s at cold start, smoother visible UX. downside: more telemetry, potential for hidden load.

carlos: we should persist an audit log for grants for 72h for postmortem and fraud detection. lightweight append-only stream OK.

zane: edge-case: cross-region session migration could double-dip. plan: include grant_id tied to session fingerprint; runtime rejects grant reuse with different region.

priya: config knobs: base_tokens (default 3), multiplier_cap (default 4), cache_ttl (30s), min_success_age (10s). make per-org overrides available for Dedicated customers.

jordan: one more: integrate with console so CS can flip whitelist to exempt orgs from caps (for onboarding demos). need RBAC.

nina: I'll author an RFC follow-up with proto, metric list, rollout checklist and the mock admission patch for integ tests. will include a small Go lib for computing cached multipliers so admission teams can share.

carlos: LGTM. can we add a telemetry tag on each request: "token_grant_id" so traces tie back to grants?

zane: yep add token_grant_id to request metadata. runtime will attach to spans.

infra-bot: deploy note: admission-service v2.5.0 -> canary 2.5% traffic scheduled for 2024-06-12 03:00 UTC.

priya: I'll coordinate SRE sync and draft alert thresholds.

nina: thanks all. will post RFC link when ready.
